title: Three News Groups Take Trump to Court Over White House Ban
summary:
Imagine you're a reporter. Your job is to ask questions and tell people what's happening. But one day, the president says you can't come inside anymore. That's what happened to three big news groups: CNN, MS NOW, and Politico.

President Trump banned them from covering events at the White House. He said he was tired of what he called unfair and negative coverage. "I don't have to let them into the people's house," he told reporters.

So the three news groups sued him. They say the ban breaks the First Amendment — that's the rule in the US Constitution that says the government can't stop people from speaking or reporting freely. They also say it breaks the Fifth Amendment, which says everyone must be treated fairly.

Their lawyer, Theodore J. Boutrous, said the ban "harms the American people, who are entitled to rigorous, fact-based coverage of the President."

The government argues that the news groups publish false information about national security. A federal judge — who was appointed by Trump — will decide. Trump has already said he'll appeal if he loses.

One funny detail: on Monday, Trump cut a ribbon on a new White House helipad. But a helicopter was so loud you couldn't hear him!
why_it_matters: Learning about the First Amendment matters to kids too, because they use free speech every day — in class debates, school newspapers, or when they speak up about something they think is unfair.

background_read: The White House is the building in Washington, D.C. where the U.S. president lives and works, and reporters have covered events there for many decades.
The First Amendment is part of the Bill of Rights, the first set of changes added to the U.S. Constitution to protect basic freedoms like speech and a free press.
Presidents and reporters have clashed before — in the 1970s, President Richard Nixon fought with the press over the Watergate scandal and later resigned.
Article_Structure: WHO: Three news groups — CNN, MS NOW and Politico — plus President Trump and his government.
WHAT: Trump banned them from covering White House events, so they sued him in court.
WHERE: The White House in Washington, D.C., and the federal court where a judge will decide.
WHY: The news groups say the ban breaks the First and Fifth Amendments, while the government says they publish false information about national security.

perspectives.description: They say the public needs reporters inside the White House to ask hard questions, and that a president should not be able to pick which news groups are allowed in.
They say the president can choose who comes into his own building and that some news groups publish unfair or false stories about national security.
They say judges usually protect press access to public places, but the exact rules can be complicated, so the case may take a long time and could be appealed.
